To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
no single treatment planning method is superior to the others for high-grade gliomas and a personalized approach to radiotherapy planning and delivery for these patients is advised.
the IMRT and TOMO plans were better than the 3D conformal plans for high grade gliomas, but that the IB plan was better than the IMRT and the TOMO plans for normal tissue sparing.
the IMRT plans had the least normal tissue sparing and the highest integral dose to the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dosimetry of four different treatment planning methods for HGG.
the dosimetry and normal tissue sparing of high-grade glioma using different radiotherapy planning techniques.
the development of a novel method for solving the inverse problem in radiation therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IB and IMRT planning techniques provide better sparing of the optic chiasm, ipsilateral globe, normal brain and the integral dose to the brain than the 3D planning technique.
IMRT plans are not inferior to other plans in terms of tumor coverage and normal brain sparing.
IMRT is superior to 3D conformal radiotherapy in terms of sparing the contralateral optic structures but not the ipsilateral structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IMRT and TOMO have better sparing of normal brain compared to 3DCRT, however, the difference is not clinically relevant.
IMRT plans with integrated boost were the most conformal and spared normal brain tissues the most, while Tomotherapy plans were the least conformal and spared the normal brain the least.
IMRT is superior to 3D conformal radiotherapy for high grade gliomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no one best planning method for HGG.
the IMRT plans are not superior to the 3DCRT plans.
the choice of radiotherapy technique is not as critical as the quality of the treatment planning process.
